safi-cedvel:4-5.t:
* I'rab:
(من وراء) attached (mutaʿalliq) to (ينادونك). (لا) is a negative particle. (الواو) is a conjunction. (لو) is a non-jussive conditional particle. (حتّى) is a particle of limit and a preposition governing the genitive. (تخرج) is an imperfect verb in the accusative (manṣūb) by an implied أن after حتّى. (إليهم) is attached to (تخرج). (اللام) occurs in the apodosis (jawāb) of لو. The noun of (كان) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun referring to the patience (الصبر) understood from the context. (الواو) is resumptive.
The interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) (أنّهم صبروا..) is in the position of nominative as the fāʿil (agent) of an omitted verb, its implied form being "ثبت" (it was established).
The interpreted maṣdar (أن تخرج..) is in the position of genitive after (حتّى), attached to (صبروا).
The clause «إنّ الذين ينادونك ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
The clause «ينادونك ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (الذين).
The clause «أكثرهم لا يعقلون ... » is in the position of nominative as the khabar (predicate) of إنّ.
The clause «لا يعقلون ... » is in the position of nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (subject) (أكثرهم).
The clause «لو (ثبت) صبرهم ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the resumptive clause.
The clause «صبروا ... » is in the position of nominative as the khabar of أنّ.
The clause «تخرج ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the implied particle maṣdar (أن).
The clause «كان خيرا ... » has no grammatical position; it is the apodosis of a non-jussive conditional.
The clause «الله غفور ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.

* Morphology:
(الحجرات) is the plural of حجرة, a name for the room that is enclosed by a wall or the like. Its pattern (wazn) is فعلة (with ḍamma then sukūn), in the sense of مفعولة (passive participle). The pattern of حجرات is فعلات (with two ḍammas).

* Rhetoric:
Kināya (metonymy): in His saying, Exalted is He, «مِنْ وَراءِ الْحُجُراتِ».
The mention of the rooms is a kināya for his seclusion, peace be upon him, with his wives, because they were set aside for them.
He did not say "the rooms of your wives", nor "your rooms", out of reverence for him ﷺ and to avoid what would cause him, peace be upon him, discomfort.

safi-cedvel:6-8.t:
* I'rab:
(جاءكم) is a past verb in the position of jussive, being the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ). (بنبإ) is attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil of جاءكم. (الفاء) links the apodosis. (أن) is a maṣdar particle governing the accusative. (بجهالة) is attached to a ḥāl from the fāʿil of تصيبوا, and (الباء) denotes accompaniment. (تصبحوا) is an incomplete imperfect verb (kāna-type), accusative, conjoined to (تصيبوا) by the فاء. (على ما) is attached to the khabar (نادمين).
The interpreted maṣdar (أن تصيبوا ... ) is in the position of accusative as a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), with an omitted muḍāf, i.e. "fearing that you strike".
The clause «النداء ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
The clause «آمنوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (الذين).
The clause «جاءكم ... » has no grammatical position; it is the response to the vocative.
The clause «تبيّنوا ... » is in the position of jussive as the apodosis, joined with the فاء.
The clause «تصيبوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the particle maṣdar (أن).
The clause «تصبحوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause تصيبوا.
The clause «فعلتم ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of (ما), whether relative noun or particle.
7- (الواو) is a conjunction. (أنّ) is a particle resembling the verb (a nāsikh). (فيكم) is attached to the khabar of أنّ. (لو) is a non-jussive conditional particle. (في كثير) is attached to (يطيع). (اللام) links the apodosis of لو. (الواو) is a conjunction in the five places. (لكنّ) is a particle of rectification governing the accusative. (إليكم) is attached to (حبّب). (في قلوبكم) is attached to (زيّنه). The second (إليكم) is attached to (كرّه). (هم) is a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl) [Note: or it is a detached pronoun, a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is الراشدون, and the clause is the khabar of أولئك ...].
The interpreted maṣdar (أنّ فيكم رسول..) is in the position of accusative, standing in place of the two objects of اعلموا.
The clause «اعلموا ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause of the response to the vocative.
The clause «يطيعكم ... » has no grammatical position; it is an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
The clause «عنتّم ... » has no grammatical position; it is the apodosis of a non-jussive conditional.
The clause «لكنّ الله حبّب ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause يطيعكم.
The clause «حبّب إليكم ... » is in the position of nominative as the khabar of لكنّ.
The clause «زيّنه ... » is in the position of nominative, conjoined to the clause حبّب.
The clause «كرّه إليكم ... » is in the position of nominative, conjoined to the clause حبّب.
The clause «أولئك هم الراشدون» has no grammatical position; it is parenthetical, or an explanatory resumption.
8- (فضلا) is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) standing in for the maṣdar, so it is a noun of the maṣdar, i.e. "He bestowed favour (تفضّل) with a favour" [Note: it may be a mafʿūl li-ajlihi whose governor is حبّب.. or whose governor is the active participle (الراشدون).], (من الله) is attached to (فضلا).
The clause « (تفضّل) فضلا ... » has no grammatical position; it is causal.
The clause «الله عليم ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the causal clause, or it is resumptive.

* Morphology:
(7) العصيان: the noun from (عصى، يعصي), of the bāb ضرب. Its pattern is فعلان (with kasra on the fāʾ and sukūn on the ʿayn), and it means abandoning obedience; or it is the maṣdar of the verb.

* Rhetoric:
1- Indefiniteness (al-tankīr): in His saying, Exalted is He, «إِنْ جاءَكُمْ فاسِقٌ بِنَبَإٍ».
In making الفاسق and النبأ indefinite there is generality across wrongdoers and reports, as if He had said: whichever wrongdoer comes to you with whichever report, then pause over it, seek clarification of the matter and the uncovering of the truth, and do not rely on people's word, because whoever does not guard against the genus of wickedness does not guard against lying, which is one kind of it. Naturally this generality and inclusiveness arise because an indefinite noun, when it occurs in a conditional context, is general, just as when it occurs in a negative context.
2- Fronting (al-taqdīm): in His saying, Exalted is He, «أَنَّ فِيكُمْ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ».
Here the khabar of أنّ is put before its noun. The benefit is the intent to rebuke some of the believers for what Allah found objectionable in them, namely that they wanted the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to follow their opinions; so it had to be put first, since the purpose is directed at it.
3- Use of the imperfect: in His saying, Exalted is He, «لَوْ يُطِيعُكُمْ».
Here He used the imperfect, not the past: He said "يطيعكم" and did not say "أطاعكم". This indicates that it was in their wish that his action should continue in line with what they considered right, and that whenever an opinion occurred to them on some matter it was acted upon, as shown by His saying «في كثير من الأمر», like your saying:
"So-and-so hosts the guest and protects the sanctuary", meaning that this is among his habits and is found in him continuously.
4- Antithesis (al-ṭibāq): in His saying, Exalted is He, «حبّب» and «كرّه».
This is a kind of antithesis, and much of it occurs in the Book of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

* Benefits:
Do not be hasty, and be clear about the matter. This verse calls us to verify reports before building any action on them, because haste often leads to regret and loss. This verse was revealed about al-Walīd ibn ʿUqba. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent him to the Banū l-Muṣṭaliq after their campaign to bring the alms. There had been enmity between him and them in the Jāhiliyya. When the people heard of him, they went out to meet him in honour of the command of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Satan whispered to him that they wanted to kill him, so he feared them and returned, and told the Prophet ﷺ that the Banū l-Muṣṭaliq had apostatised and come out to fight him. The Prophet ﷺ sent Khālid ibn al-Walīd. Khālid reached them and stayed hidden, and heard the call to the maghrib and ʿishāʾ prayers, and saw them to be people of obedience and piety. He collected the zakāh from them and asked them about their coming out toward al-Walīd, and they said: "We came out to receive him." Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed this verse.

safi-cedvel:9-10.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) is resumptive. (طائفتان) is the fāʿil of an omitted verb that what follows explains, i.e. "اقتتلت طائفتان" (two groups fought). (من المؤمنين) is attached to an adjective (naʿt) of (طائفتان). (الفاء) links the apodosis. (بينهما) is an adverb (ẓarf) in the accusative attached to (أصلحوا). (الفاء) is a conjunction. (بغت) is a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on an implied fatḥa on the alif that was dropped because of the meeting of two sukūns, in the position of jussive, being the protasis. (على الأخرى) is attached to (بغت). (الفاء) links the apodosis. (التي) is a relative noun in the position of accusative as the mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and it is an adjective of an implied modified noun, i.e. "the group which..". (حتّى) is a particle of limit and a preposition governing the genitive. (تفيء) is an imperfect verb in the accusative by an implied أن after حتّى. (إلى أمر) is attached to (تفيء).
The interpreted maṣdar (أن تفيء..) is in the position of genitive after (حتّى), attached to (قاتلوا).
(الفاء) is a conjunction. (إن فاءت) is like إن بغت. (فأصلحوا بينهما) is like the first. (بالعدل) is a ḥāl from the fāʿil of أصلحوا.
The clause « (اقتتلت) طائفتان ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
The clause «اقتتلوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is explicative.
The clause «أصلحوا ... » is in the position of jussive as the apodosis, joined with the فاء.
The clause «بغت إحداهما ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the resumptive clause.
The clause «قاتلوا ... » is in the position of jussive as the apodosis, joined with the فاء.
The clause «تبغي ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (التي).
The clause «تفيء ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the implied particle maṣdar (أن).
The clause «فاءت ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause بغت ...
The clause «أصلحوا (the second) ... » is in the position of jussive as the apodosis, joined with the فاء.
The clause «أقسطوا ... » is in the position of jussive, conjoined to the clause أصلحوا.
The clause «إنّ الله يحبّ ... » has no grammatical position; it is causal.
The clause «يحبّ ... » is in the position of nominative as the khabar of إنّ.
10- (إنّما) consists of a restraining particle and the restrained one (kāffa and makfūfa). (الفاء) links the apodosis of an implied condition. (أصلحوا بين..)
is like the first, and (الواو) in (ترحمون) is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent).
The clause «المؤمنون إخوة ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
The clause «أصلحوا (the third) ... » is in the position of jussive as the apodosis of an implied condition, i.e. "if they fight, then make peace ...".
The clause «اتّقوا ... » is conjoined to the last clause أصلحوا.
The clause «لعلّكم ترحمون» has no grammatical position; it is an explanatory resumption, or causal. The clause «ترحمون» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of لعلّ.

* Morphology:
(بغت) involves an iʿlāl (weak-letter change) by deletion, because of the meeting of two sukūns, the lām of the word and the tāʾ of feminine marking.

* Rhetoric:
1- Eloquent simile (al-tashbīh al-baligh): in His saying, Exalted is He, «إِنَّمَا الْمُؤْمِنُونَ إِخْوَةٌ», where they are likened to brothers in that they are traced to one origin, namely faith, which brings about eternal life. It may also be an isti'āra (metaphor) and a likening of sharing in faith to sharing in the origin of procreation, because each of the two is an origin of survival: procreation is the source of life, and faith is the source of eternal survival in the Gardens.
2- Specification (al-takhṣīṣ): in His saying, Exalted is He, «فَأَصْلِحُوا بَيْنَ أَخَوَيْكُمْ».
Here the two are singled out for mention rather than the plural, because the fewest between whom discord can occur is two; so if reconciliation is required between the fewest, it is more required between the many, since the harm in the discord of a group is greater than in the discord of two.
3- Putting the overt noun in place of the pronoun: in His saying, Exalted is He, «فَأَصْلِحُوا بَيْنَ أَخَوَيْكُمْ».
Here the overt noun is put in place of the pronoun, annexed to the addressees, to stress emphatically the obligation of reconciliation and the singling out for it.

* Benefits:
- The ruling on fighting the rebels (al-bughāt)..
The scholars said: In these two verses there is evidence that rebellion does not remove the name of faith, because Allah, Exalted is He, called them believing brothers despite their being rebels. Supporting this is what is reported from ʿAlī, may Allah be pleased with him, who is the model in fighting the people of rebellion. He was asked about the people of the Camel: "Are they polytheists?" He said: "No, they fled from polytheism." It was said: "Are they hypocrites?" He said: "No, the hypocrites remember Allah only a little." It was said: "Then what is their state?" He said: "Our brothers who rebelled against us." In the sharia, the rebel (al-bāghī) is the one who rises against the just imam. If a group having strength and protection gathers, refuses obedience to the just imam and sets up an imam for themselves, then the ruling concerning them is that the imam sends to them and calls them to obey him. If they show a grievance, he removes it from them; if they mention no grievance and persist in rebellion, the imam fights them until they return to his obedience. The ruling on fighting them then is that "their fleeing one is not pursued, their captive is not killed, and their wounded one is not finished off (yudhaffaf, i.e. dispatched)", as the herald of ʿAlī proclaimed on the day of the Camel. And whatever one of the two groups destroys of the other, in life and property, during the fighting, there is no liability on it. As for those who do not combine these three conditions, such as being a small group with no protection, or having no interpretation (taʾwīl), or not having set up an imam, they are not to be confronted so long as they do not initiate fighting and do not molest the Muslims. If they do that (that is, initiate fighting and molest the Muslims), they are in ruling like highway robbers.

safi-cedvel:11-11.t:
* I'rab:
(لا) is a prohibitive particle governing the jussive. (من قوم) is attached to (يسخر). (عسى) is a complete past verb. (أن) is a maṣdar particle governing the accusative. (منهم) is attached to (خيرا).
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يكونوا..) is in the position of nominative as the fāʿil of عسى. (الواو) is a conjunction. (لا) is like the first. (نساء) is the fāʿil of an omitted verb that what precedes explains, i.e. "لا يسخر نساء.." (let women not mock). (من نساء) is attached to the implied verb. (عسى أن يكنّ خيرا منهنّ) is like عسى أن يكونوا خيرا منهم, and (يكنّ) is an incomplete imperfect verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on sukūn, in the position of accusative..
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يكنّ..) is in the position of nominative as the fāʿil of the second عسى.
(الواو) is a conjunction in the three places. (لا) is a prohibitive particle governing the jussive in the two places. (بالألقاب) is attached to (تنابزوا). (الفسوق) is the khabar of an obligatorily omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being "هو" (it is), and it is the one specified for censure (al-makhṣūṣ bi-l-dhamm) [Note: or it is a postponed mubtadaʾ whose khabar is the preceding clause of censure ... and al-Maḥallī allowed that it be a badal (substitute) from the noun, with the one specified for censure omitted.], (بعد) is an adverb (ẓarf) in the accusative attached to (الفسوق). (من) is a conditional noun governing the jussive, a mubtadaʾ. (لم) is for negation only. (يتب) is jussive, the protasis. (الفاء) links the apodosis. (هم) is a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl) [Note: or a detached pronoun, a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is الظالمون, and the clause is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (أولئك).].
The clause «النداء ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
The clause «آمنوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (الذين).
The clause «لا يسخر قوم ... » has no grammatical position; it is the response to the vocative.
The clause «عسى أن يكونوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is causal.
The clause «يكونوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the particle maṣdar (أن).
The clause « (لا يسخر) نساء ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause of the response to the vocative.
The clause «عسى أن يكنّ ... » has no grammatical position; it is causal.
The clause «يكنّ ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the particle maṣdar (أن).
The clause «لا تلمزوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause of the response to the vocative.
The clause «لا تنابزوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause of the response to the vocative.
The clause «بئس الاسم ... » has no grammatical position; it is parenthetical.
The clause « (هو) الفسوق ... » is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl from the noun.
The clause «من لم يتب ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause of the response to the vocative.
The clause «لم يتب ... » is in the position of nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (من) [Note: it is possible that the khabar is the two clauses, protasis and apodosis, together.].
The clause «أولئك هم الظالمون» is in the position of jussive as the apodosis, joined with the فاء.

* Morphology:
(يكنّ) involves an iʿlāl by deletion, because of the indeclinability on sukūn when the nūn of the feminine plural enters. Its origin is يكونن, with a quiescent nūn followed by a vowelled nūn; two sukūns met, so the wāw was dropped and it became يكنّ, after the two nūns were assimilated. Its pattern is يفلن.
(تنابزوا): one of the two tāʾs was dropped from it; its origin is تتنابزوا.
(الألقاب) is the plural of لقب, a name for what a person is called, other than his first name, indicating elevation or lowliness. Its pattern is فعل (with two fatḥas), and the pattern of ألقاب is أفعال.

* Rhetoric:
The secret of the plural: in His saying, Exalted is He, «لا يَسْخَرْ قَوْمٌ مِنْ قَوْمٍ عَسى أَنْ يَكُونُوا خَيْراً مِنْهُمْ وَلا نِساءٌ مِنْ نِساءٍ». He did not say "a man of a man" or "a woman of a woman" in the singular, in order to announce that more than one of their men, and more than one of their women, venture into mockery, and to treat as monstrous the state they were in. For the scene of a mocker scarcely lacks someone who amuses himself and laughs at his words and does not do what he owes by way of forbidding and denouncing, and so becomes a partner of the mocker and follows him in bearing the sin. Likewise everyone whose ear it reaches, who finds it pleasant and laughs at it. That leads, even if one person produced it, to a multiplication of mockery and the turning of one into a group and a people.
Indefiniteness (al-tankīr): in His saying, Exalted is He, «لا يَسْخَرْ قَوْمٌ مِنْ قَوْمٍ ... وَلا نِساءٌ مِنْ نِساءٍ».
Here He made القوم and النساء indefinite, because every group is forbidden, with itemisation among the groups and with the prohibition addressing each group in particular. With definiteness the prohibition would be achieved, but not by itemisation, rather by inclusion; and prohibition by itemisation is more eloquent and has more impact.

* Benefits:
- Noble character..
This verse was revealed for three reasons..
1- His saying, Exalted is He: «يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لا يَسْخَرْ قَوْمٌ مِنْ قَوْمٍ عَسى أَنْ يَكُونُوا خَيْراً مِنْهُمْ». Ibn ʿAbbās said: It was revealed about Thābit ibn Qays ibn Shammās. He had a heaviness in his ear, so when he came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and they had already taken the seats, or they made room for him until he sat beside him and could hear what he said. One day he arrived after missing one rakʿa of the dawn prayer. When the Prophet ﷺ finished and he found no seat, he stood where he was. When Thābit finished the prayer, he went toward the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, stepping over the necks of the people, saying: "Make room." They began making room for him until he reached the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, with one man between him and him. He said: "Make room." The man said to him: "You have got a seat, so sit." Thābit sat behind him, angry. When the darkness lifted, Thābit nudged the man and said: "Who is this?" He said: "I am so-and-so." Thābit said to him: "Son of so-and-so's mother", mentioning a mother of his for whom he was taunted in the Jāhiliyya. The man bowed his head and was ashamed, and Allah revealed this verse.
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: It was revealed about the delegation of Banū Tamīm, who used to ridicule the poor Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
2- The second reason is His saying, Exalted is He: «وَلا نِساءٌ مِنْ نِساءٍ عَسى أَنْ يَكُنَّ خَيْراً مِنْهُنَّ». It is reported from Anas that it was revealed about the wives of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who taunted Umm Salama for her shortness. And from Ibn ʿAbbās that it was revealed about Ṣafiyya bint Ḥuyayy: some of the Prophet's ﷺ wives said to her: "A Jewess, daughter of two Jews."
3- And the third reason is His saying, Exalted is He: «وَلا تَلْمِزُوا أَنْفُسَكُمْ وَلا تَنابَزُوا بِالْأَلْقابِ».
From Abū Jabīra ibn al-Ḍaḥḥāk, the brother of Thābit ibn al-Ḍaḥḥāk al-Anṣārī, who said: This verse was revealed about us, the Banū Salima. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came to us, and there was not a man among us without two or three names. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ would say "O so-and-so", and they would say: "Stop, O Messenger of Allah, he is angered by that name." Then Allah revealed this verse.
Some scholars said: What is meant by these nicknames is what the one addressed dislikes, or what conveys blame of him. As for nicknames that have become like proper names for their owners, such as al-Aʿmash and al-Aʿraj and the like, there is no harm in them if the person called by them does not dislike them. And nicknames that earn praise and commendation, and are true and sincere, are not disliked. The whole matter turns on disparaging a person and detracting from him: if the nickname conveys that, it is forbidden; otherwise not.

safi-cedvel:12-12.t:
* I'rab:
(يأيّها الذين آمنوا): its parsing has already been given, in words and clauses [Note: in verse (1) of this sūra.]. (من الظنّ) is attached to an adjective (naʿt) of (كثيرا). (الواو) is a conjunction. (لا) is a prohibitive particle governing the jussive in the two places. (تجسّسوا) is a jussive imperfect verb from which one of the two tāʾs was dropped. (الهمزة) is for rhetorical (disapproving) interrogation. (أن) is a maṣdar particle governing the accusative. (ميتا) is a ḥāl from أخيه, accusative. (الفاء) links the apodosis of an implied condition, and (الواو) in (كرهتموه) is redundant (zāʾida), a lengthening of the vowel of the mīm..
The clause «اجتنبوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is the response to the vocative.
The clause «إنّ بعض الظنّ إثم ... » has no grammatical position; it is causal.
The clause «لا تجسّسوا» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause of the response to the vocative.
The clause «لا يغتب بعضكم ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause of the response to the vocative.
The clause «يحبّ أحدكم ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
The clause «يأكل ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the particle maṣdar (أن).
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يأكل..) is in the position of accusative as the direct object.
The clause «كرهتموه ... » is in the position of nominative as the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being "هذا" (this)..
The nominal clause is the apodosis of an implied condition, i.e. "if you do not like that, then this you have disliked".
The clause «اتّقوا الله ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to an implied resumption, i.e. "so dislike suspicion, spying and backbiting, and fear Allah".
The clause «إنّ الله توّاب ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.

* Rhetoric:
1- Indefiniteness (al-tankīr): in His saying, Exalted is He, «كَثِيراً».
Its coming indefinite conveys the sense of partiality, and that among suspicions there are some that must be avoided, without specifying or identifying them, so that no one ventures upon a suspicion except after looking and reflecting, and distinguishing its truth from its falsehood by a clear sign, while keeping a sense of piety and caution. Had it been definite, the command to avoid suspicion would have been tied to that of it which is frequent and not to that which is rare, and every suspicion characterised by frequency would have to be avoided, while that characterised by rarity would be permitted.
2- Representational metaphor (al-istiʿāra al-tamthīliyya): in His saying, Exalted is He, «أَيُحِبُّ أَحَدُكُمْ أَنْ يَأْكُلَ لَحْمَ أَخِيهِ مَيْتاً فَكَرِهْتُمُوهُ».
In this noble verse there is a representation and depiction of what the backbiter inflicts on the honour of the one backbitten, in the most horrible and most repulsive way.
It contains various intensifications: among them the interrogation whose sense is affirmation; among them making what is utterly detestable to be linked with love; among them attributing the act to "one of you" and indicating that not one of all individuals likes that; among them that He did not stop at representing backbiting by eating a human's flesh, but made the human a brother; and among them that He did not stop at eating the brother's flesh, but made him dead.

* Benefits:
- The prohibition of backbiting (ghayba)..
This verse indicates the prohibition of backbiting,
for it is reported from Abū Hurayra, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Do you know what backbiting is?" I said: "Allah and His Messenger know best." He said:
"Your mentioning your brother with what he dislikes." I said: "And if what I say is in my brother?" He said: "If what you say is in him, you have backbitten him; and if what you say is not in him, you have slandered him."
From ʿĀʾisha, may Allah be pleased with her, who said: I said to the Prophet ﷺ: "It is enough for you about Ṣafiyya that she is such and such." Some narrators said: she meant short. He said: "You have said a word that, if it were mixed with the water of the sea, would taint it." From Anas, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "When I was taken up, I passed by a people who had nails of copper, scratching their faces and their chests. I said: 'Who are these, O Jibrīl?' He said: 'These are those who eat people's flesh and plunge into their honour.'"
This verse was revealed about two men who backbit their companion. When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ went on a campaign or a journey, he would join a needy man to two well-off men, to serve them and eat with them. Salmān was with two men serving them; sleep overcame him and he did not prepare food for them. They said: "Go to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and ask him for food for us." Salmān came and asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who told Usāma to look for food for him, but he found none. He went back to the two, and they said: "Usāma was stingy." They sent him to a group of the Companions and he found nothing. When he returned, they said: "Had we sent him to the well of Sumayḥa, its water would have sunk." Then they went off spying to see whether Usāma had food or not. When he came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, he said to them: "Why do I see the greenness of meat in your mouths?" They said: "O Messenger of Allah, we have not eaten any meat today." He said: "You have been eating the flesh of Salmān and Usāma." Then this verse was revealed.

safi-cedvel:13-13.t:
* I'rab:
(يأيّها الناس) is like يأيّها الذين.. [Note: in verse (1) of this sūra.], and the following here is verbal (lafẓiyya). (من ذكر) is attached to (خلقناكم). (شعوبا) is the second direct object, accusative. (اللام) is for cause, or the lām of consequence. (تعارفوا) is an imperfect verb in the accusative by an implied أن after the lām, with one of the two tāʾs dropped from it..
The interpreted maṣdar (أن تعارفوا..) is in the position of genitive by the lām, attached to (جعلناكم).
(عند) is an adverb (ẓarf) in the accusative attached to (أكرمكم)..
The clause «النداء ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
The clause «إنّا خلقناكم ... » has no grammatical position; it is the response to the vocative.
The clause «خلقناكم ... » is in the position of nominative as the khabar of إنّ.
The clause «جعلناكم ... » is in the position of nominative, conjoined to the clause خلقناكم.
The clause «تعارفوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the implied particle maṣdar (أن).
The clause «إنّ أكرمكم ... أتقاكم» has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
The clause «إنّ الله عليم ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.

* Morphology:
(شعوبا) is the plural of شعب, a collective noun for the whole of the people. It is said that it was so named because the tribes branch out (tashaʿʿub) from it. Its pattern is فعل (with fatḥa then sukūn), and the pattern of شعوب is فعول (with ḍamma on the fāʾ).
(قبائل) is the plural of قبيلة, of the pattern فعيلة, a collective noun with no singular from its own wording; they are the children of one father.
(أكرمكم) is a comparative/superlative (ism tafḍīl) from the triliteral كرم, its pattern being أفعل.
(أتقاكم) is an ism tafḍīl from the triliteral وقى, its pattern being أفعل, and it involves the substitution of tāʾ for wāw, following the substitution in the quinquiliteral form.. then the change remained; the original is أوقى. Or it is from the triliteral تقى يتقي of the bāb ضرب, with maṣdars تقى (with ḍamma on the tāʾ), تقاء (with kasra) and تقية.. in the sense of اتّقى; so the substitution arises from the origin, starting from the triliteral, or there is no substitution at all. See further explanation and detail in verse (13) of Sūrat Maryam under the word (تقيّ).

safi-cedvel:14-15.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) is a conjunction. (لكن) is for rectification, with no government. (الواو) is circumstantial (ḥāliyya). (يدخل) is an imperfect verb jussive by (لمّا), and it is vowelled with kasra because of the meeting of two sukūns. (في قلوبكم) is attached to (يدخل). (الواو) is a conjunction, or resumptive. (لا) is a negative particle. (يلتكم) is a jussive imperfect verb, the apodosis. (من أعمالكم) is attached to (يلتكم). (شيئا) is the second direct object, accusative..
The clause «قالت الأعراب ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
The clause «آمنا ... » is in the position of accusative as the content of what is said (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «قل ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
The clause «لم تؤمنوا ... » is in the position of accusative as the content of what is said.
The clause «قولوا ... » is in the position of accusative, conjoined to the clause لم تؤمنوا [Note: there is an omission in the speech; the original is: "You have not believed, so do not say 'we believe', but you have submitted, so say 'we have submitted' ...". In the science of badīʿ this is called iḥtibāk.].
The clause «أسلمنا ... » is in the position of accusative as the content of what is said.
The clause «لمّا يدخل الإيمان ... » is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl.
The clause «تطيعوا ... » is in the position of accusative, conjoined to the clause لم تؤمنوا [Note: if the clause is not part of the speech dictated to the Prophet, peace be upon him, it is resumptive.].
The clause «لا يلتكم ... » has no grammatical position; it is the apodosis not joined with the فاء.
The clause «إنّ الله غفور ... » has no grammatical position; it is causal.
15- (إنّما) consists of a restraining particle and the restrained one. (الذين) is a relative noun in the position of nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (المؤمنون). (بالله) is attached to (آمنوا). (بأموالهم) is attached to (جاهدوا). (في سبيل) is attached to (جاهدوا). (هم) is a pronoun of separation [Note: or a detached pronoun, a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is الصادقون, and the nominal clause is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (أولئك).].
The clause «المؤمنون الذين ... » has no grammatical position; it is an explanatory resumption.
The clause «آمنوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (الذين).
The clause «لم يرتابوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the ṣila clause.
The clause «جاهدوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the ṣila clause.
The clause «أولئك ... الصادقون» has no grammatical position; it is a resumption confirming the content of what precedes.

* Morphology:
(يلتكم) involves an iʿlāl by deletion because of the jussive. It is the imperfect of a mithāl (assimilated, initial weak) verb; لاته means "he diminished it". Its pattern is يعلكم (with fatḥa, kasra, sukūn).

* Rhetoric:
The art of rectification (al-istidrāk): in His saying, Exalted is He, «قالَتِ الْأَعْرابُ آمَنَّا قُلْ لَمْ تُؤْمِنُوا وَلكِنْ قُولُوا أَسْلَمْنا». Here the clause «لم تؤمنوا» sufficed in place of saying "do not say 'we believe'", since it is objectionable that they be addressed with an expression whose import is forbidding them to speak of faith. Then the clause headed by the word of rectification was joined to it, carried on the sense. He did not say "but you have submitted", so that it comes out in the mode of claim and assertion, as their saying «آمنا» was. Had He said "but you have submitted", it would have come out as conceding it to them and counting their statement as valid, whereas it is not to be counted.

* Benefits:
- The negative jussive (لما)..
It is specific to the imperfect: it puts it in the jussive, negates it and turns it to the past, like لم, except that it differs from it in five matters:
1- It is not joined with a conditional particle, so one does not say "إن لما تقم". In the Revelation: (وَإِنْ لَمْ تَفْعَلْ) (وَإِنْ لَمْ يَنْتَهُوا).
2- What it negates continues to be negated up to the present, as in the saying of al-Mumazzaq al-ʿAbdī: (فإن كنت مأكولا فكن خير آكل ... وإلا فأدركني ولما أمزّق) (If I am to be eaten, then be the best of eaters; otherwise reach me before I am torn apart.)
whereas what is negated by لم may be connected to the present, as in His saying (وَلَمْ أَكُنْ بِدُعائِكَ رَبِّ شَقِيًّا). For this reason it is allowed to say "لم يكن ثم كان" (he was not, then he was), but not "لما يكن ثم كان"; rather you say "لما يكن وقد يكون" (he has not yet been, but he may be).
3- What is negated by لما is only close to the present, and this is not required for what is negated by لم. You say: "لم يكن زيد في العام الماضي مقيما" (Zayd was not resident last year).
4- What is negated by لما is expected to occur, unlike what is negated by لم. Do you not see that the meaning of (بَلْ لَمَّا يَذُوقُوا عَذابِ) is that they have not tasted it up to now, and that their tasting it is expected? Al-Zamakhsharī said on His saying, Exalted is He, «وَلَمَّا يَدْخُلِ الْإِيمانُ فِي قُلُوبِكُمْ»: since the sense of (لما) is expectation, it indicates that these people did believe afterwards. For this reason they allowed "لم يقض ما لا يكون" but prevented it with (لما). This difference is with respect to the future; with respect to the past the two are alike in negating the expected and the non-expected. An example of the expected: you say "مالي قمت ولم تقم", or "ولما تقم". An example of the non-expected: you say at the outset "لم تقم", or "لما تقم".
5- What is negated by (لما) may be omitted, as in the saying of Dhū l-Rumma:
(فجئت قبورهم بدءا ولما ... فناديت القبور فلم يجبنه) (I came to their graves as a leader, and not yet [a leader before that]... I called to the graves and they did not answer him)
meaning "ولما أكن بدءا قبل ذلك" (and I had not been a leader before that), i.e. a chief. It is not permitted to say "وصلت إلى بغداد ولم تريد ولم أدخلها" [Translator's note: the source text reads "ولم تريد", which appears garbled; translated as written, and the intended sense is evidently that لم, unlike لما, does not allow omission of its negated verb.].
The reason for all these rulings is that لم is for negating "he did" (فعل), and لما is for negating "he has done" (قد فعل).

safi-cedvel:16-16.t:
* I'rab:
(الهمزة) is for rhetorical (disapproving) interrogation. (بدينكم) is attached to (تعلّمون) [Note: in the sense of "make known" or "inform".]. (الواو) is circumstantial. (في السموات) is attached to an omitted element which is the ṣila of ما, and likewise (في الأرض) for the second relative. (بكلّ) is attached to the khabar (عليم).
The clause «قل ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
The clause «تعلّمون ... » is in the position of accusative as the content of what is said.
The clause «الله يعلم ... » is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl.
The clause «يعلم ... » is in the position of nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (الله).
The clause «الله ... عليم» is in the position of accusative, conjoined to the ḥāl clause [Note: or it is resumptive, with no grammatical position.].

safi-cedvel:17-17.t:
* I'rab:
(عليك) is attached to (يمنّون). (أن) is a maṣdar particle [Note: or a lightened form of the heavy one, its noun an omitted pronoun and the clause after it a khabar.
(4, 5) It is possible that it be in the position of genitive by an omitted preposition, namely the bāʾ, attached to the preceding verb ...].
The interpreted maṣdar (أن أسلموا) is in the position of accusative as a direct object, its governor being يمنّون «4».
(لا) is a prohibitive particle governing the jussive. (عليّ) is attached to (تمنّوا). (بل) is for transitional abandonment (iḍrāb). (عليكم) is attached to (يمنّ). (أن) is like the first. (للإيمان) is attached to (هداكم). (كنتم) is a past verb in the position of jussive, the protasis..
The interpreted maṣdar (أن هداكم..) is in the position of accusative as a direct object, its governor being يمنّ «5».
The clause «يمنّون» has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
The clause «أسلموا ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the particle maṣdar (أن).
The clause «قل ... » has no grammatical position; it is an explanatory resumption.
The clause «لا تمنّوا ... » is in the position of accusative as the content of what is said.
The clause «الله يمنّ ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
The clause «يمنّ عليكم ... » is in the position of nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (الله).
The clause «هداكم ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the second particle maṣdar (أن).
The clause «كنتم صادقين» has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.. The apodosis is omitted, indicated by what precedes, i.e. "then Allah confers favour upon you.." or "then Allah is the one conferring favour upon you".

safi-cedvel:18-18.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) is a conjunction in the two places. (ما) is a maṣdar particle [Note: or a relative noun in the position of genitive, with the returning pronoun omitted, and the clause its ṣila.]..
The interpreted maṣdar (ما تعملون) is in the position of genitive by the bāʾ, attached to the khabar (بصير).
The clause «إنّ الله يعلم ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
The clause «يعلم ... » is in the position of nominative as the khabar of إنّ.
The clause «الله بصير ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the resumptive clause.
The clause «تعملون ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the particle maṣdar (ما).

safi-cedvel:1-1.t:
* I'rab:
(أيّها) is a vocative, a specific indefinite noun, indeclinable with ḍamma in the position of accusative. (الذين) is a relative noun, a badal from أيّ - or an ʿaṭf bayān of it - in the position of accusative. (لا) is a prohibitive, jussive particle. (بين) is an accusative adverb attached to (تقدّموا)..
The clause: «يأيّها الذين آمنوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is an opening clause (ibtidāʾiyya).
The clause: «آمنوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (الذين).
The clause: «لا تقدّموا ... » has no grammatical position; it is the response to the vocative.
The clause: «اتّقوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the response to the vocative.
The clause: «إنّ الله سميع ... » has no grammatical position; it is an explanatory resumption.

* Rhetoric:
1- Representational metaphor (istiʿāra tamthīliyya): in His words, the Exalted, «لا تُقَدِّمُوا بَيْنَ يَدَيِ اللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ».
A representational metaphor, for passing judgement decisively without following or obeying the one whom it is obligatory to follow, depicting its ugliness and foulness by a sensory image in what they were forbidden, like the servant going ahead in front of his master as he walks, where there is no benefit. What is meant: do not settle a matter, be categorical about it and dare to commit it before Allah the Exalted and His Messenger ﷺ have ruled on it and given permission for it.
2- Omission: in His words, the Exalted, «لا تُقَدِّمُوا».
Here the object of تقدّموا is omitted, for two reasons: one: that it is omitted so as to cover everything that comes to mind of what might be put forward; the second: that no object is intended, nor its omission, and the prohibition is directed at the act of advancing itself, as though it were said: "Do not engage in this act, and do not let it have any path to you", like His words, the Exalted: «هُوَ الَّذِي يُحْيِي وَيُمِيتُ».

safi-cedvel:2-3.t:
* I'rab:
(لا) is a prohibitive, jussive particle. (فوق) is an accusative adverb attached to (ترفعوا). (الواو) is a conjunction. (لا) is like the first. (له) is attached to a ḥāl from the agent of تجهروا. (بالقول) is attached to (تجهروا). (كجهر) is attached to an omitted absolute object [Note: or to an omitted ḥāl.]. (لبعض) is attached to (جهر). (أن) is a maṣdar and accusative particle. (الواو) is the wāw of circumstance (ḥāliyya). (لا) is negative.
The clause: «يأيّها الذين ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
The clause: «آمنوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (الذين).
The clause: «لا ترفعوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is the response to the vocative.
The clause: «لا تجهروا ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the response to the vocative.
The clause: «تحبط أعمالكم ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the particle-type relative (أن).
The interpreted maṣdar (أن تحبط) is in the position of accusative as an object of purpose, with an omitted muḍāf, i.e. "for fear that your deeds be nullified".
The clause: «أنتم لا تشعرون» is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl.
The clause: «لا تشعرون» is in the position of nominative as the predicate of the mubtadaʾ (أنتم).
3- (عند) is an accusative adverb attached to (يغضّون). (أولئك) is a mubtadaʾ whose predicate is (الذين) [Note: it is permissible for (الذين) to be an adjective of the demonstrative - or a badal - and the clause «لهم مغفرة» the predicate.]. (للتقوى) is attached to (امتحن), with an omitted muḍāf, i.e. "for the manifestation of piety". (لهم) is attached to a fronted predicate of the mubtadaʾ (مغفرة)..
The clause: «إنّ الذين يغضّون ... » has no grammatical position; it is causal.
The clause: «يغضّون ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (الذين).
The clause: «أولئك الذين ... » is in the position of nominative as the predicate of inna.
The clause: «امتحن الله ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the second relative noun (الذين).
The clause: «لهم مغفرة ... » has no grammatical position; it is an explanatory resumption [Note: or in the position of nominative as a second predicate of (إنّ).].

* Rhetoric:
Repetition (takrīr): in His words, the Exalted, «يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا».
The repetition of the address to them is a summons to them to renew their insight at every incoming address, to refresh their attentiveness to every revealed ruling, and a stirring so that they do not slacken and become heedless of their reflection and of what they were held to on attending the assembly of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, of the courtesy whose habitual observance is of great benefit in their religion.

* Benefits:
- Courtesy towards the elder..
In this verse Allah commanded the believers not to raise their voices above the voice of the Prophet ﷺ, and to lower their voices in his presence, because raising the voice is contrary to modesty, dignity and respect.
When this verse was revealed, Thābit ibn Qays sat in his house and said: I am one of the people of the Fire. And he stayed away from the Prophet ﷺ. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ asked Saʿd ibn Muʿādh and said: O Abū ʿAmr, what is the matter with Thābit? He said: He is my neighbour, and I know of no complaint of his. He said: So Saʿd went to him and told him what the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had said. Thābit said: This verse was revealed, and you know that I am one of the loudest of you in voice before the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, so I am one of the people of the Fire. Saʿd mentioned that to the Prophet ﷺ, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "He is one of the people of Paradise." In another report he added: "Are you not pleased to live praiseworthy, to be killed a martyr, and to enter Paradise?" He said: I am pleased with the glad tidings of Allah and His Messenger; I shall never raise my voice above the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Then Allah revealed إِنَّ الَّذِينَ يَغُضُّونَ أَصْواتَهُمْ عِنْدَ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ. We used to look at a man of the people of Paradise walking among us, and on the day of al-Yamāma, in the war against Musaylima, he died a martyr, may Allah be pleased with him.
